radiology_report:
Radboudumc Diagnostic Imaging | 10 January 2025 | Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate

Clinical context: Assessment of rising PSA (7.4 ng/mL) alongside a previously Negative biopsy.

FINDINGS:
Prostatic dimensions yield a total volume of 45.0 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a faint, poorly circumscribed intermediate-signal focus (roughly 12 x 8 mm) within the right mid-gland peripheral zone. Diffusion-weighted imaging exhibits mild restriction with corresponding ADC hypointensity, yet lacks profound restriction. Dynamic contrast-enhancement demonstrates early, non-specific uptake without a rapid washout profile. Seminal vesicles appear normal. There is no evidence of extraprostatic extension or suspicious lymphadenopathy.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 3 lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone.
Prostate volume 45.0 mL; PSA density 0.16 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.61967.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial laboratory screening recorded a PSA of 4.6 ng/mL, which increased to 5.0 ng/mL on a December 2023 repeat test; the upward trend at his age triggered a urology referral. Current pharmacotherapy manages hypertension and atrial fibrillation, and he notes only mild urinary frequency without significant discomfort.
